acceptance_criteria.criterion: The severity validation guard in the error log REST route accepts 'audit' and 'info' as valid values, using a Set-based lookup pattern as specified in the plan.
All three credential-audit append() callsites in src/server/routes/config.ts use Severity: 'audit'.

All existing tests in config.test.ts and repositories.test.ts that previously asserted Severity: 'warning' on credential-audit entries now assert Severity: 'audit'.

All existing tests pass after changes.

comments.note: The VALID_SEVERITIES Set in error-log.ts is allocated on every request. For clarity and micro-efficiency it could be lifted to module scope as a constant. Low priority — allocation cost is negligible and the current placement keeps it visually adjacent to where it is used.

The WP spec referenced '3 callsites in config.ts' but the actual codebase has only 2 (PUT create/update and DELETE). The third appears to have been addressed in a prior plan cycle. No action needed — the actual code is correct.

The comment on line 177 of config.ts (JSDoc for registerConfigRoutes) previously said Severity: 'warning'; updated to 'audit' to stay in sync. Consider adding the full severity type reference ('audit') to the inline route comment block inside the GET /api/error-log handler as well — the inline docs at lines 32-34 of error-log.ts were also updated to list all four values.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified. ErrorSeverity type union confirmed as 'error' | 'warning' | 'audit' | 'info'. Set-based severity guard validated — accepts all 4 values, silently rejects invalid values (e.g. 'critical'). config.ts has 2 credential-audit append() callsites (not 3 as spec stated — developer note confirmed), both use Severity: 'audit'. repositories.ts has 1 callsite at line 306 using Severity: 'audit'. config.test.ts has 3 assertions at lines 1636, 1662, 1681 using Severity: 'audit'. repositories.test.ts has 2 assertions at lines 676, 700 using Severity: 'audit'. No remaining 'warning' assertions on credential-audit entries. New error-log.test.ts tests at lines 153 and 177 verify audit/info severity filtering with proper total count assertions. All 921 tests pass; TypeScript compiles cleanly with no errors.

comments.note: AC3 spec/code discrepancy confirmed: WP spec states 3 callsites in config.ts but only 2 exist (lines 318 and 363). grep of append() in config.ts returns exactly 2 hits. This is a stale spec issue from a prior plan cycle — both present callsites are correctly migrated to Severity: 'audit'. No action required.

The VALID_SEVERITIES Set in error-log.ts (line 90) is constructed inside the request handler on every call. This is functionally correct but allocates on each request. Module-scope constant would eliminate per-request allocation. Negligible in practice given Node.js V8 optimization, but worth noting for future housekeeping.

No tests cover the ErrorLogManager.list() filtering logic directly against the actual storage layer for 'audit' and 'info' severities (only the route layer is tested via the mock manager). The manager-level filtering for these new severity values relies on the existing generic filter path. Low risk given the implementation pattern, but integration-level coverage would add depth.
